findings.title: Cache status stays stale after a successful cache delete
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation's `onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. It never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`, unlike the disconnect mutation, which does so in `onSettled`. `onChanged` is often undefined, and the query uses `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. As a result, after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the delete option until a full reload, so it looks like the delete did nothing.

findings.title: Plain Error instead of TRPCError for not-found/forbidden
findings.body: Throwing a generic `Error` when the credential doesn't belong to the user makes tRPC return an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). It also gets logged as a server fault. Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` so clients get a proper 4xx response and logs aren't polluted.

findings.title: Extra no-op updateMany on every cache refresh
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`, which fires on each Google webhook. With empty `data`, whether Prisma bumps `updatedAt` at all is unreliable. Per the PR notes, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere; the UI reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This adds a write across all selected calendars of the credential on a hot path for no functional benefit and should be removed.

findings.title: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the surrounding string is translated. Non-US users will see US-style dates (MM/DD/YY, 12h clock) inside localized text. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (i18n.language) instead.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired entries
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows regardless of `expiresAt`. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. The UI can therefore show a cache as present and "last updated" when every entry is expired and nothing would actually be served from cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`.

findings.title: Migration warning contradicts the SQL; legacy rows get misleading timestamp
findings.body: The header warns that the column is added "without a default value", but the statement does use `DEFAULT NOW()`. That stale autogenerated comment should be removed. Also, every existing cache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`, so the UI will report legacy caches as freshly updated at deploy time.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only; ENV_FILE path depends on cwd
findings.body: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD sed. On Linux, GNU sed treats `''` as a filename and the update fails. In addition, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory rather than the script's location, so running it from the repo root writes to the wrong file.

findings.title: dev:cron depends on undeclared tsx via npx
findings.body: `npx tsx` relies on `tsx`, which is not declared in dependencies. npx will download it on demand, which can prompt or fail in offline or CI environments and leaves the version unpinned. `ts-node` is still in devDependencies. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency or keep `ts-node`.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId
findings.body: `getConnectedDestinationCalendars` is re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries`. Widening the required Pick fields on the input type forces every external caller (e.g. API v2) to select `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars. Otherwise their type check breaks, yet these fields are never used by this function.

findings.title: No tests for new handler or repository method
findings.body: There are no unit tests for `deleteCacheHandler`, including its ownership check and the case of a credential belonging to another user. There are also none for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or for the cache enrichment in `connectedCalendarsHandler`. The PR itself notes it was never tested end-to-end.
